title: Proof and procedural limits in Contracts cases
shortTitle: Proof and procedural limits in Contracts cases
summary: A case’s procedural posture determines which facts are assumed, which are established, and what the court’s ruling actually resolves.
notes: A dismissal decision can test pleaded allegations without finding them true. Summary judgment asks whether the relevant record requires a trial. An appellate remand may permit a theory while leaving factual questions unresolved. Read these distinctions alongside D&G Stout, Dorton, and the damages cases; a successful appeal does not necessarily establish ultimate liability or a particular award.
